heard: NASA pointed Voyager 1 right back at the sun. Blinding sunlight risked destroying its cameras nearly 4 billion miles out. Astronomer Carl Sagan had spent years begging NASA to turn around. Voyager 1 was tilted about 32 degrees above the planet's plane. Engineers snapped 60 frames using their darkest filter and fastest shutter. Mercury and Mars were lost, but 6 distant planets appeared. Those final photographs became our first family portrait from the outside. No camera had ever looked back toward home.
